title: bool() of a symbolic value refuses while recording, as float() does
author: Claude-JG
description: revision2026c step RG12.49.6 (decided: first a way to still use the if): a Python if on a symbolic comparison is decided once while recording, with the values of the arguments then (zero in CreateSymbolicUserFunction), and records only that branch, silently. bool() shall raise a TypeError while recording, with a message that names both ways that exist: exudyn.symbolic.IfThenElse(condition, a, b), decided at every evaluation, and x.Evaluate() or x.value, decided once at recording, explicitly; before that, the recordings of the test models and examples are checked for an if or a library function that reads bool() of a symbolic value.
releaseNotes: A Python if, and, or, not on a symbolic value (exudyn.symbolic.Real) raises a TypeError while recording, which names exudyn.symbolic.IfThenElse for a decision at each call and Evaluate() for a decision at recording; before, Python took every symbolic value as true, so a recorded function took the first branch for every call. A symbolic number, and a comparison with recording off, are conditions by their value.
